userStories.title: Split a diff into whole-readable parts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the pure splitter that preserves the whole branch diff in ordered, whole-readable parts.

**Motivation** — The branch review should judge the branch as a whole.

**Approach** — **Splitting (US-001).** `splitDiffIntoParts(diff: string): readonly DiffPartText[]`, with `DiffPartText = { text: string; files: readonly string[] }`, is a pure function over `git diff` text:

- The diff is cut into per-file sections at each line starting with `diff --git `. The diff is run with `--no-renames` and `-c core.quotePath=false`, so the line reads `diff --git a/<path> b/<path>` with the same path twice; a section's file is that path, taken as the first `(length - 3) / 2` characters after `diff --git a/`. A header whose path git still quotes (it starts with `"`) has no file: the section is packed as usual and adds nothing to `files`.
- A diff line longer than `DIFF_PART_MAX_LINE_CHARS` (1 900) characters is wrapped before packing into lines of at most 1 900 characters; every line after the first starts with `\ continued: `. A part therefore never holds a line the `Read` tool would cut at `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS` (2 000).
- A section's header is its lines from `diff --git` up to, not including, its first line starting with `@@`. A section with no `@@` line (a binary or mode-only change) is all header.
- Sections are packed greedily in diff order: a section joins the current part while the part stays at or under `DIFF_PART_MAX_BYTES` (32 000) UTF-8 bytes and `DIFF_PART_MAX_LINES` (900) lines; otherwise the current part closes and the section starts the next part.
- A section over either limit on its own is cut into pieces, and each piece is a part of its own: no other section joins it, and the next section starts a new part. The section is cut before its `@@` lines, consecutive hunks staying together while the piece fits, so each such piece is the header followed by whole hunks, each with its own `@@` line. A single hunk that does not fit is cut at line boundaries; every piece of it is the header, then that hunk's `@@` line, then the next run of the hunk's lines. The header and the repeated `@@` line count toward the piece's limits.
- A part's `files` are the files of the sections or pieces it holds, in order, without repeats; a file cut into pieces is in the `files` of every part that holds one of its pieces.
- An empty diff yields `[]`.

**Scope** — In: new branch-diff-parts.ts pure types/constants/splitting and focused split tests. Out: filesystem/git part writing (US-002), audit credit (US-003), prompt/op wiring (US-004), one-session dispatch (US-005), slicing deletion (US-006); no ceiling on the total branch diff size.

**Interface**
```typescript
type DiffPartText = { text: string; files: readonly string[] };
splitDiffIntoParts(diff: string): readonly DiffPartText[]
```
Export DIFF_PART_MAX_BYTES = 32_000, DIFF_PART_MAX_LINES = 900 and DIFF_PART_MAX_LINE_CHARS = 1_900. Test pure packing, repeated headers/hunk markers, prefix-inclusive line wrapping and lossless reconstruction in packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/branch-diff-parts-split.test.ts before implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] splitDiffIntoParts("") returns [].
[unit] splitDiffIntoParts returns one part for a diff of two files of a few lines each, a.ts then b.ts.
[unit] For the two-small-file diff, the returned part's files equals ["a.ts", "b.ts"].
[unit] For the two-small-file diff, the returned part's text equals the input diff.
[unit] For a diff of 40 files of 2 000 bytes each, every part's text is at most DIFF_PART_MAX_BYTES (32 000) UTF-8 bytes.
[unit] For a diff of 40 files of 30 lines each, every part's text is at most DIFF_PART_MAX_LINES (900) lines.
[unit] For a diff of files that all fit the limits, the parts' text joined in order equals the input diff.
[unit] For a file whose section has three hunks of 15 000 bytes each, splitDiffIntoParts returns at least two parts.
[unit] For that three-hunk file, each part holding its hunks starts its text with that file's header lines.
[unit] For that three-hunk file, every part holding one of its hunks includes the file in files.
[unit] For that three-hunk file followed by a small file, the small file starts a new part instead of joining the large file's last piece.
[unit] For a single hunk of 2 000 lines, every emitted piece has at most 900 lines, header and repeated @@ line included.
[unit] For that 2 000-line hunk, every piece's text is the file's header, then the hunk's @@ line, then hunk lines.
[unit] For a diff line of 5 000 characters, splitDiffIntoParts writes three lines of at most 1 900 characters, the second and third starting with \ continued: .
[unit] For the header diff --git a/dir with space/a.ts b/dir with space/a.ts, the section's file is dir with space/a.ts.
[unit] A section whose header path is quoted (diff --git "a/q\"x.ts" "b/q\"x.ts") adds nothing to its part's files.
[unit] The exported limits equal { DIFF_PART_MAX_BYTES: 32_000, DIFF_PART_MAX_LINES: 900, DIFF_PART_MAX_LINE_CHARS: 1_900 }.

routing.reasoning: The byte/line/hunk packing algorithm is nontrivial but pure, fully specified and confined to one new module, so focused failing tests can drive implementation in one session.

suggestedCriteria: For a diff containing multibyte UTF-8 characters, every emitted part remains at or below 32 000 UTF-8 bytes.
For a mode-only section without an @@ line that fits both budgets, the returned text preserves the complete section.
When multiple sections name the same file in one part, that part's files includes the file only once.
When an input diff has no final newline and needs no wrapping or splitting, the returned part's text equals that input exactly.

userStories.title: Write the diff parts beside the branch package
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Materialize the complete branch diff as numbered files beside the branch package and append their file inventory.

**Motivation** — The real cause of #2858 was a package with no diff in it.

**Approach** — **Writing (US-002).** `writeBranchDiffParts(projectDir, from, packagePath): Promise<DiffPart[]>`, with `DiffPart = { path: string; files: readonly string[] }`, runs one `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --text --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames --unified=10 <from>..HEAD -- . <ALWAYS_EXCLUDED>` through `_workflowDeps.git` (the flags and pathspec the static-mode patch already uses), splits it with `splitDiffIntoParts`, and writes each part next to the package as `<stem>-part-<NN>.diff`, where `<stem>` is the package file name without `.diff` (`package-branch` for `package-branch.diff`) and `<NN>` is the 1-based part number zero-padded to two digits, or to three when there are more than 99 parts. Before writing, it deletes every `<stem>-part-*.diff` already in the package directory, so an earlier review of the same run leaves no stale part. It then appends to the package a section headed `## Diff parts (<N>)` with one line per part: `- <absolute part path>: <file>, <file>`. File-system calls go through a new `_branchDiffPartsDeps = { list, remove, write }` seam (list the package directory's file names, delete one file, write one file).

Failure behavior: a non-zero git diff exit throws NaxError code WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED. A stale-part deletion failure throws the same code before any part is written. An empty diff writes no part, returns [] and still appends ## Diff parts (0). Reuse ALWAYS_EXCLUDED from @/review and keep external diff/textconv disabled.

**Scope** — In: extend US-001's branch-diff-parts.ts with DiffPart, injectable list/remove/write and the writer; mocked seam tests and temporary-git integration tests. Out: tool-read credit (US-003), prompt/retry consumption (US-004), calling the writer from runBranchReview and readingNote (US-005), slicing/config removal (US-006). `nax bot review` keeps its current package (no diff parts) and its current coverage rules; `writeBranchReviewPackage` without the new option behaves as today.

**Interface**
```typescript
type DiffPart = { path: string; files: readonly string[] };
writeBranchDiffParts(projectDir, from, packagePath): Promise<DiffPart[]>
_branchDiffPartsDeps = { list, remove, write }
```
Use the pure splitter from US-001 rather than another packing implementation. All returned part paths and package inventory paths are absolute. Keep matching cleanup scoped to the exact package stem; complete cleanup before writes. Add tests in packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/branch-diff-parts-write.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] In a temporary git repository with a seed commit and a second commit changing a.ts and b.ts, writeBranchDiffParts(repo, seed, <dir>/package-branch.diff) writes <dir>/package-branch-part-01.diff.
[integration] For that two-file repository, writeBranchDiffParts returns one DiffPart with path equal to that absolute part path and files equal to ["a.ts", "b.ts"].
[integration] For that two-file repository, the part file holds every line the second commit added to a.ts.
[integration] For that two-file repository, the package file ends with a section headed ## Diff parts (1) whose line names the part's absolute path and a.ts, b.ts.
[integration] When a changed path is in ALWAYS_EXCLUDED, no returned part's files includes that path.
[unit] With _workflowDeps.git returning a diff that splits into 3 parts, the written part names are package-branch-part-01.diff, package-branch-part-02.diff and package-branch-part-03.diff.
[unit] With a diff that splits into 120 parts, the first and last written part names are package-branch-part-001.diff and package-branch-part-120.diff.

[unit] With _branchDiffPartsDeps.list returning ["package-branch-part-07.diff", "other.diff"], writeBranchDiffParts calls _branchDiffPartsDeps.remove only for package-branch-part-07.diff, not other.diff.
[unit] When _branchDiffPartsDeps.remove throws, writeBranchDiffParts throws a NaxError with code WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED.
[unit] When _branchDiffPartsDeps.remove throws, _branchDiffPartsDeps.write is never called.
[unit] When _workflowDeps.git returns exit code 128 for the diff, writeBranchDiffParts throws a NaxError with code WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED.
[unit] When the diff is empty, writeBranchDiffParts returns [].
[unit] When the diff is empty, writeBranchDiffParts writes no part file.
[unit] When the diff is empty, writeBranchDiffParts appends a section headed ## Diff parts (0) to the package.

routing.reasoning: Standard git and filesystem integration extends one module using established dependency seams; main risks are cleanup ordering, error wrapping and path/number formatting.

suggestedCriteria: When stale parts outnumber the new parts, successful writeBranchDiffParts leaves no obsolete higher-numbered part files for that package stem.
When the package directory is outside projectDir, writeBranchDiffParts still returns absolute paths in that package directory.

userStories.title: Credit whole reads of diff parts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Derive file inspection credit from complete audited reads of every diff part holding a file.

**Motivation** — The fix that keeps the whole branch in one session is to give the reviewer the whole diff, uncut, in pieces it can read whole.

**Approach** — **Part credit (US-003).** `toolReadParts(calls: readonly ToolCallRecord[], parts: readonly DiffPart[]): string[]` returns, in part order without repeats, the files whose every holding part was shown whole by a `Read` call: `tool: "Read"`, `outcome: "ok"`, `truncated: false`, `resultBytes <= TOOL_READ_CREDIT_MAX_BYTES`, no `offset` and no `limit`, and `input.path` equal to the part's absolute path. These are the gates the private `creditedPaths` applies; `toolReadParts` applies them itself. The part path is compared as-is, because the run directory may sit outside the repository, where `normalizeReviewPath` drops it. `ToolCallRecord` is the type `@nathapp/nax-agent` exports.

**Scope** — In: extend branch-diff-parts.ts with the pure toolReadParts helper and credit tests. Out: changing creditedPaths/readSessionToolCalls or agent audit production, retry credit (US-004 remains self-report only), final review integration (US-005). Part credit and coverage-retry part names for a file whose path git quotes in the `diff --git` header (a double quote, backslash or control character in the path); such a file is still credited by the reviewer's own `inspectedFiles`. Part credit for ACP sessions: their tool-audit rows carry no `truncated` field, so they earn no part credit, as they earn no tool-read credit today.

**Interface**
```typescript
toolReadParts(calls: readonly ToolCallRecord[], parts: readonly DiffPart[]): string[]
```
Use TOOL_READ_CREDIT_MAX_BYTES (40_000) from review-tool-reads.ts; do not export or alter its private creditedPaths. The common AC fixture has parts [{ path: "/run/package-branch-part-01.diff", files: ["a.ts"] }, { path: "/run/package-branch-part-02.diff", files: ["a.ts", "b.ts"] }]. Unless overridden, calls are Read, outcome ok, truncated false, resultBytes 30_000 and have no offset or limit. Add tests in packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/branch-diff-parts-credit.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] For the common two-part fixture, toolReadParts returns ["b.ts"] when the only whole successful Read names /run/package-branch-part-02.diff.
[unit] For the common two-part fixture, toolReadParts returns ["a.ts", "b.ts"] when whole successful Reads name both parts.
[unit] A Read call with offset: 1 earns no toolReadParts credit.
[unit] A Read call with limit: 100 earns no toolReadParts credit.
[unit] A Read call with truncated: true earns no toolReadParts credit.
[unit] A Read call with no truncated field earns no toolReadParts credit.
[unit] A Read call with outcome: "error" earns no toolReadParts credit.
[unit] A Read call with resultBytes: 40_001 earns no toolReadParts credit.
[unit] A Git call whose input names /run/package-branch-part-02.diff earns no toolReadParts credit.

routing.reasoning: One additive pure helper filters existing audit records and aggregates holding-part sets; it neither opens sessions nor changes authentication, permissions or session lifecycle.

suggestedCriteria: A whole successful Read with resultBytes: 40_000 earns credit for files whose every holding part has been read.
Repeated successful Reads of the same part do not duplicate any file in toolReadParts' return value.
A relative Read path does not credit a part whose path is absolute, even when their basenames are equal.
toolReadParts returns [] when calls is empty or parts is empty.

userStories.title: Name diff parts in the branch prompt and coverage retry
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give the reviewer whole-diff reading instructions and route unread-file retries to the corresponding part names.

**Motivation** — The reviewer then has to choose which files to open, and on large branches it opened 13 of 58.

**Approach** — **Prompt and coverage retry (US-004).** `BranchReviewPromptInput` gains `diffParts?: readonly DiffPart[]`. When it is non-empty, `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt` describes the package as "commits, --stat, changed files and the list of diff parts" and puts `buildBranchDiffPartsNote(parts)` where the pull-each-file note was: a `## How to read the diff` section saying the parts hold the whole branch diff with 10 lines of context, listing every part's absolute path, and telling the reviewer to Read every part whole and in order, with no `offset` or `limit`, to open a changed file itself only for context the diff does not show, and to list in `inspectedFiles` every file whose diff it read. With `diffParts` absent or empty the prompt is byte-for-byte today's. `workflowBranchReviewOp`'s input gains `diffParts?: readonly DiffPart[]`; the op turns it into a map from file to part file names and passes it to `buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry` as the new optional `partsOf`. With `partsOf`, the retry tells the reviewer to Read whole the part named beside each file, and lists each unread file as `- <file> (<part file name>[, <part file name>])`; a file absent from the map is listed as today. The retry stays in the same session with the same `workflow.review.coverageRetries` budget. Its `missing` list stays the self-reported `inspectedFiles` comparison: tool-audit credit is read only after the session ends (the audit file is flushed at hop end), so it shortens the final unread list, never a retry.

**Scope** — In: prompt builder/input, new exported buildBranchDiffPartsNote, optional op input, part-basename map and retry-builder plumbing; new prompt tests and existing op integration tests. Out: audit-credit computation (US-003), dispatch/package/verdict wiring (US-005), deleting slice input/line (US-006). Part credit inside a coverage retry: tool-audit credit is read after the session ends and shortens only the final unread list. `nax bot review` keeps its current package (no diff parts) and its current coverage rules; `writeBranchReviewPackage` without the new option behaves as today.

**Interface**
```typescript
// BranchReviewPromptInput and workflowBranchReviewOp input:
diffParts?: readonly DiffPart[]
buildBranchDiffPartsNote(parts)
buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(range, missing, staticMode = false, progress?, partsOf?: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly string[]>)
```
Export buildBranchDiffPartsNote through @/prompts. Keep the existing parse retry, coverage progress/stagnation budget and incomplete-verdict retention unchanged. Only type references to the workflow DiffPart contract should cross into operations/prompts; avoid adding runtime workflow dependencies. Add packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/workflow-branch-builder-parts.test.ts; extend existing test/unit/operations/workflow-branch-review.test.ts or workflow-branch-review-coverage.test.ts for a real callOp/agent-stub retry. No LLM call is added.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt with two diffParts returns a prompt whose ## How to read the diff section names both parts' absolute paths.
[unit] With those two diffParts, the reading section tells the reviewer to Read every part whole and in order, without offset or limit.
[unit] With those two diffParts, the prompt does not include This package holds no diff.
[unit] With those two diffParts, the prompt describes the package as commits, --stat, changed files and the list of diff parts.
[unit] buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt with diffParts: [] returns the same text as with diffParts absent.

[unit] buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry("s..HEAD", ["a.ts"], false, { attempt: 1, max: 3 }, new Map([["a.ts", ["package-branch-part-03.diff"]]])) returns a prompt with the line - a.ts (package-branch-part-03.diff).
[unit] For that mapped retry, the prompt tells the reviewer to Read whole the part named beside each file.
[unit] With partsOf holding a.ts in package-branch-part-01.diff and package-branch-part-02.diff, the retry line is - a.ts (package-branch-part-01.diff, package-branch-part-02.diff).
[unit] With partsOf that lacks b.ts, the retry line for b.ts is - b.ts.
[unit] buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry without partsOf returns the same text it returns today for the same arguments.

[integration] When callOp invokes workflowBranchReviewOp with diffParts holding a.ts in /run/package-branch-part-02.diff, requiredFiles ["a.ts"] and an agent stub whose first reply omits a.ts from inspectedFiles, the second prompt includes - a.ts (package-branch-part-02.diff).

routing.reasoning: Optional input fields, conditional prompt text and a basename map extend established builders and the existing retry callback without changing session lifecycle or security policy.

userStories.title: Run one branch-review session over the whole diff
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace per-slice dispatch with one whole-branch review call, materialize diff parts and combine self-reported/direct/part inspection evidence.

**Motivation** — Its remit is cross-story integration, contracts between packages and reachability, which only a reviewer that sees the whole branch can judge.

**Approach** — **The package's reading note (US-005).** `writeBranchReviewPackage` gains `readingNote?: boolean` (default `true`). When `staticMode` is not `true` and `readingNote` is `false`, the package is written without the "## How to read the diff" note. `staticMode: true` writes the full patch section as today and ignores `readingNote`. `nax bot review` passes neither option change and keeps today's package.

**One session (US-005).** `runBranchReview` writes the package with `readingNote: false`, calls `_branchReviewDeps.writeBranchDiffParts`, classifies the required set as today, and makes exactly one `callOp` of `workflowBranchReviewOp` inside one `underReviewLimit`, with `requiredFiles` the whole required set and `diffParts` the written parts (absent when there are none). After the call it reads the session's tool calls once with `readSessionToolCalls` (the query `observedToolReads` builds today) and derives both `toolReadPaths(calls, projectDir)` and `toolReadParts(calls, parts)` from them. The unread set is the required files not covered by the self-reported `inspectedFiles`, the tool reads, or the part reads. The verdict carries `diffParts: { part: <part file name>; files }[]` when at least one part was written, and neither `diffParts` nor `slices` otherwise.

Failure behavior: when writeBranchDiffParts throws WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED, return { ran: false } with why and never call the op, matching existing package failures via reviewPackageFailure. When the diff is empty, the writer appends ## Diff parts (0), the op gets no diffParts and the prompt retains today's reading note. If the tool audit cannot be read, readSessionToolCalls supplies no calls, so only self-reported inspection counts in the absence of other audit evidence. Ranged or cut part reads earn no credit. Keep abort propagation and timeout/unparseable failure semantics.

**Scope** — In: add the writer to _branchReviewDeps, write package/parts once, invoke one op with all required files, load calls once, add basename diffParts metadata, compute final unreadFiles, readingNote options, and corresponding tests. Out: deleting remaining obsolete slice module/types/config/prompt line (US-006), changing the pure splitter/writer/credit contracts (US-001/002/003), changing retry coverage from self-reported inspectedFiles (US-004). `nax bot review` keeps its current package (no diff parts) and its current coverage rules; `writeBranchReviewPackage` without the new option behaves as today. The branch fix re-review package (`package-branch-fix.diff`, written by `writeReviewPackage` through `truncateDiff`) is unchanged. Part credit inside a coverage retry: tool-audit credit is read after the session ends and shortens only the final unread list.

**Interface**
```typescript
writeBranchReviewPackage(projectDir, from, path, options?: { staticMode?: boolean; readingNote?: boolean }): Promise<string[]>
_branchReviewDeps = { writeBranchReviewPackage, writeBranchDiffParts, reviewRequiredFiles }
// BranchReviewVerdict:
diffParts?: readonly { readonly part: string; readonly files: readonly string[] }[]
```
Seams: US-002's writeBranchDiffParts is consumed through _branchReviewDeps; US-003's toolReadParts and US-004's prompt/op input are consumed by the seeded runBranchReview trigger used by branchReviewStep through FeatureEnv.steps.branchReview after its !rec.seed guard. Preserve story reports, rules/project-context appends, memory, model selection and existing draft gating. Take sinceMs before the call and reuse observedToolReads' auditDir/runId/ledgerSessionName/sinceMs query and missing-runId/outputDir guards, but derive both evidence forms from the single loaded calls list. Never mutate the op verdict's inspectedFiles. Keep one workflow.timeouts.reviewMs (default 30 minutes) for the one review session, including retries.

Create packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/branch-review-diff-parts.test.ts. Rewrite multi-session/merge assertions in branch-review-sliced.test.ts to one-session behavior or delete assertions that pin only slicing; retain applicable package/abort/timeout regression assertions. Update branch-review-tool-reads.test.ts to one scripted reply and one audit load for both credit forms. Update pr-step-context.test.ts to assert ## Diff parts (1) and a part line naming change.txt rather than the in-package git diff command. Extend real-git package tests for readingNote false/default/static precedence.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] runBranchReview calls _branchReviewDeps.writeBranchDiffParts once with the project dir, review seed and run dir's package-branch.diff path when that dependency is stubbed.
[unit] With 40 required files, writeBranchDiffParts returning 3 stubbed parts and _workflowDeps.callOp stubbed, runBranchReview calls callOp exactly once with workflowBranchReviewOp.
[unit] For that 40-file review, the op input's requiredFiles holds all 40 files.

[unit] When the session's tool audit yields no calls and inspectedFiles omits a.ts, the verdict's unreadFiles includes a.ts.
[unit] With 3 parts written, the verdict's diffParts lists each part's file name and files, in order.
[unit] With 3 parts written, the verdict has no slices field.

[unit] When writeBranchDiffParts returns [], the op input has no diffParts field.
[unit] When writeBranchDiffParts returns [], the prompt includes git diff <seed>..HEAD -- <path>.
[unit] When writeBranchDiffParts throws WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED, runBranchReview returns ran: false.
[unit] When writeBranchDiffParts throws WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED, runBranchReview returns a why explaining the package failure.
[unit] When writeBranchDiffParts throws WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED, runBranchReview never calls callOp.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module review-session orchestration changes dispatch/timeout boundaries and audited evidence aggregation while preserving bot/static behavior; strict three-session TDD applies to the session-related implementation.

suggestedCriteria: When both direct-file reads and part reads are credited, runBranchReview loads the audit once after callOp resolves.
When a whole direct-file Read credits a.ts that inspectedFiles omits, runBranchReview removes a.ts from unreadFiles without adding it to inspectedFiles.
When writeBranchDiffParts returns [], the verdict has no slices field.
When the sole review call returns null, runBranchReview returns { ran: false, why: "unparseable reply" }.

the review runs one session, not one per slice; tests that script one reply per slice script one reply, and the tool-call stub is read once for both tool-read and part credit.

the branch package is written with `readingNote: false`, so `git diff ${base}..HEAD -- <path>` is no longer in `package-branch.diff`; assert instead that the package holds `## Diff parts (1)` and a part line naming `change.txt`.

userStories.title: Remove branch-review slicing and retire sliceFiles
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Delete the obsolete slicing surface and warn-and-strip workflow.review.sliceFiles while retaining coverageRetries.

**Motivation** — The owner's ruling (2026-11-13): the branch review is not sliced.

**Approach** — **Removal (US-006).** `branch-review-slices.ts` (`planReviewSlices`, `mergeSliceVerdicts`, `SliceResult`), the `BranchReviewSlice` type, the verdict's `slices` field, the prompt input's `slice` field and its prompt line, `runSlice`, and the `workflow.review.sliceFiles` schema field, runtime type field and config description are deleted. `workflow.review.sliceFiles` is added to `REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS` with the hint `the branch review is no longer split into slices; it reads the whole branch diff in one session`.

**Scope** — In: obsolete slice code/types/re-exports/prompt/config removal, removal warning registration, and updating affected runtime fixtures/assertions. Out: implementing part splitting/writing/credit/prompt wiring (US-001 through US-004) or changing the integrated whole-branch review from US-005. Removing `workflow.review` or `workflow.review.coverageRetries`. Stripping `workflow.review.sliceFiles` from project or profile configs; no checked-in nax config sets it, and the removal warning names it for any that does. The exact limits are 32_000 UTF-8 bytes, 900 logical lines and 1_900 characters per emitted line, including continuation prefixes. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/truncate.ts:28-30 supplies the larger model caps (40_000 bytes, 1_000 lines, 2_000 UTF-16 line characters); its :23 documents Read's extra [N lines] header. Split file sections before packing; parse repeated unquoted a/path b/path halves rather than splitting on spaces; quoted headers have no attributable file. Greedy packing must honor both byte and line budgets. Oversized sections are isolated from neighbors; repeat headers and hunk markers as specified without losing hunk content. Unicode byte size, continuation-prefix overhead, trailing newline line counting, and metadata-only/header-heavy sections are the principal splitter risks. The spec does not define a special fallback for a header that itself cannot fit with a hunk marker; do not silently truncate or invent a new feature policy. outOfScope: The branch review keeps one `workflow.timeouts.reviewMs` (default 30 minutes) for its one session, coverage retries included, where each slice used to get its own; a branch that needs longer raises that key.

Part credit and coverage-retry part names for a file whose path git quotes in the `diff --git` header (a double quote, backslash or control character in the path); such a file is still credited by the reviewer's own `inspectedFiles`.
`nax bot review` keeps its current package (no diff parts) and its current coverage rules; `writeBranchReviewPackage` without the new option behaves as today.
The branch fix re-review package (`package-branch-fix.diff`, written by `writeReviewPackage` through `truncateDiff`) is unchanged.
No ceiling on the total branch diff size: a branch whose parts do not fit the reviewer's context is left to coverage, and files it did not read keep the PR a draft as today.
Part credit inside a coverage retry: tool-audit credit is read after the session ends and shortens only the final unread list.
Part credit for ACP sessions: their tool-audit rows carry no `truncated` field, so they earn no part credit, as they earn no tool-read credit today.
Deduplicating restated cannot-verify items beyond today's exact-text merge; with one session the carried list is restated once.

Starved CI checks (#2889) are a separate feature.
